architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: Explicit requirements are a contemporary tropical waterfront mansion in Saint Lucia, a flat site, exceptional luxury ambition associated with the US$25m value context, a distinctive entrance, beautiful living spaces, private bedroom wings, purposeful upper-level architecture, and integrated outdoor living. The price is treated as an ambition/context signal rather than an area formula. Assumptions: the water outlook is toward local +Z and landward arrival is from -Z; exact sun, storm, access-road, setback, survey, and shoreline data are unknown. The residence is intentionally substantial rather than compact: a broad one-level public base is paired with a quieter upper suite and lounge, preserving a low, sheltered tropical profile while creating a dramatic two-level estate composition.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: A limestone arrival walk approaches from -Z to a recessed bronze door under a deep canopy. The entry opens into the central living hall, with the public sequence continuing directly through view glazing to the covered waterside terrace, pool deck, and waterfront outlook. The west ground wing is set aside for private guest bedrooms, while the elevated east suite is reached by an explicit internal stair and upper landing. The kitchen/service zone is placed on the arrival-side east edge of the public hall, adjacent to dining and separated from bedroom circulation.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: The primary volume is the 16m by 13m, 3m-high central living hall centered at [0,0.2,0.5], with its roof datum at approximately Y=3.2. A lower, 8m by 10m west bedroom wing centered at [-12,0.2,1] is subordinate and quieter. The upper east suite is a deliberately set-back 10m by 8m volume over the eastern half of the principal hall, supported by the principal enclosure and an internal support wall; its floor datum is Y=3.2 and roof datum is Y=6.5. A shallow, full-width waterside loggia extends the primary living datum toward +Z without competing with the main volumes.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: The assumed water view is toward +Z. The central living room faces the water through a series of wide, independently articulated glazed bays, while opaque side walls provide furniture surfaces and privacy. A covered terrace is directly connected to the living room and continues as a dry pool deck around a rectangular basin. The detached open pavilion is placed beyond the pool on the same deck datum for a sheltered waterfront lounge. The upper suite faces the water and is protected by its own terrace railing; the ground bedroom wing looks laterally outward rather than across public entertaining space.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: A composition of deep flat roof planes gives the estate a calm, horizontal tropical identity: the main ivory roof has a generous perimeter overhang, while the upper roof is set back and slimmer. Limestone grounds the arrival, pool coping, and selected walls; bronze defines doors, glazing, and slender structure. Facades use a deliberate rhythm of solid piers and separately sized glazed bays rather than a continuous glass curtain. Timber screens shade the exposed west bedroom frontage and timber soffits warm the loggias. Roof drainage, waterproofing, hurricane detailing, and corrosion resistance are not simulated.
